entries.core_move: Test Fourier-integral convergence for continuous-time signals and LTI impulse responses to recognize when frequency-response analysis on the $j\omega$ axis must be extended with Laplace-domain exponential weighting.

entries.lesson_title: Signals Whose Fourier Transform Does Not Converge
entries.core_move: Determine whether a continuous-time signal lacks a convergent Fourier transform by testing the Fourier-transform integral for convergence and interpreting nondecaying or growing behavior as requiring Laplace-domain exponential weighting.

Apply exponential weighting to a continuous-time signal to determine how multiplying by $e^{-\sigma t}$ can make a nonconvergent Fourier-transform integral converge and motivate the Laplace-domain variable $s=\sigma+j\omega$.

Convert an exponentially weighted Fourier integral into Laplace-domain notation by identifying $s=\sigma+j\omega$, with $\sigma$ setting the convergence-producing exponential weight and $\omega$ setting the sinusoidal frequency.

entries.lesson_title: Laplace Transform as a Generalization of Fourier Transform
entries.core_move: Interpret $X(s)$ as the Fourier transform of $x(t)e^{-\sigma t}$, identifying the ordinary Fourier transform as the $\sigma=0$ specialization when convergence permits.
Map each complex value $s=\sigma+j\omega$ onto the $s$-plane and interpret $\sigma$ as exponential weighting and $\omega$ as the Fourier-frequency coordinate.
Determine the region of convergence by using exponential weighting to identify the set of $s$-plane values for which a signal's Laplace-transform integral converges.
